name: rill
//: THE GRAMMAR IS THE TOKENIZER, TRANSCRIBED. Every rule below has a line in
`src/parser.zig`'s `tokenize` (:230) behind it, and where the two could
disagree the comment says which line. A highlighter that guesses at a
grammar is a second, quieter parser that drifts from the first one; this
one is meant to be checkable against the real tokenizer, and the gates in
`test/` run it over all 47 corpus programs.
WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO — three of them, each for the same
reason: the operator registry is OPEN (host-injected, `src/registry.zig`),
so no static list can be right.
1. It does not know the operator set. A word in HEAD position (the start
of a statement, or after a `|`) is scoped as an operator whether it
is `perish`, matryoshka's `drift`, or a local `as` name being piped.
Colouring the third one as a verb is the price of never being wrong
about the first two, and a chain reads as a chain either way.
2. It does not know which ops are TWO WORDS. `rbf …` is rill core's only
two-word family and is spelled out; a host's (`drift spawn`, `light
move`) gets its verb scoped and its sub-op left as an argument. No
lexical rule can separate `drift spawn` from `along track` — see
#operator-head-two-word.
3. It does not know which ports are TAILS (§3.11). A tail captures the
rest of the line VERBATIM from raw source, and only the registry
knows a port is one, so a locator (`/tmp/loop.wav`,
`pack:horns#audio.stem`) is highlighted as ordinary argument tokens.
That is close to plain text and never mangles the line — except for a
locator holding `//`, which reads as a comment. rill's OWN tokenizer
does the same thing outside a tail, so the grammar is faithful; it is
the tail's exemption it cannot see. Gated in test/grammar.test.mjs.
`//` opens a comment and `#` does not — ruled 2026-08-25, and the
reason is that `#` is the tag sigil (`#garrison`) and cannot also lead
a comment. A plain `//` match is exactly rill's rule and not an
approximation of it: `/` is name-INTERIOR only when it JOINS two name
characters, so `render/grade/exposure` lexes as one word (see
#bare-word, which carries the same joiner) and no `//` can ever sit
inside a token. Every `//` the tokenizer meets is at a boundary, by
construction.
comment.name: comment.line.double-slash.rill

//: The ONE concession to the tail port, and it is a concession the
tokenizer cannot contradict: a `/` that does not JOIN two name
characters has no meaning in rill at all. It is an inert `raw` token,
legal only inside a tail (§3.11) — so a `/`-led run in argument
position is a locator, is text rather than structure, and is scoped as
text. `/tmp/loop.wav` comes out whole instead of shattering into a
stray slash, a joined name and a projection.
It stops at whitespace and at `|`, so it can only ever claim the run
the author typed, and it sits AFTER #comment so `// …` is still a
comment. The blind spot it does not fix is a locator holding `//`
(`https://…`): rill's own tokenizer reads that as a comment outside a
tail, and a grammar that disagreed with the tokenizer to be helpful
would be the second, quieter parser this file exists not to be.
locator.name: string.unquoted.locator.rill

string.//: The tokenizer takes the raw span between quotes and applies escapes later; a newline inside one is `unterminated string`, so this rule stays on its line.
string.name: string.quoted.double.rill

patterns.//: `using <tokens…> as :name` binds a parse-time fold (§3.10). `use` is still reserved so the parser can point at `using`; it is scoped as the keyword it is, and rill will tell him the rest.
patterns.name: keyword.control.using.rill

patterns.//: `also { … }` is fan-out spelled inline — pure desugaring, no new node kind.
patterns.name: keyword.control.also.rill

//: `as` names an edge. Two spellings, and the difference is the sigil:
`as :k` closes a `using` and binds a FOLD; `as tangent` binds a stream.
The bound name gets a definition scope so the outline and the eye find
it in the same place.
`:name` is ONE token, colon included, exactly as `$chan` is. What
decides is ADJACENCY, not position (`colonOpensFold`, parser.zig:213):
every other colon in the language glues to the name on its LEFT — a
port type `x: number`, a record `{l: 0.28}`, a kwarg `at: row.pos` —
and a fold colon glues to the name on its RIGHT. So the whitelist
below is the tokenizer's: start of line, whitespace, or one of
`:k.tight` is therefore `:k` + a projection, and it is scoped that way
— NOT as a path. The head has no `plane`/`row`/`slate` scope on it,
because a fold is tokens, not a store: it may hold a path prefix
(`using plane.drift.@self.k as :k`) and it may hold anything else.
A number GLUED to a unit is one token (§3.13). The unit set is closed
and ratified — s, ms, m, f — so an unknown one is loud here for the
same reason it is loud in the parser (`unknown duration unit '5x'`)
rather than splitting quietly into a number and a name.
`(?:\.\d+)?` stops short of `..` on its own: the range separator is
two dots and `\d` matches neither, so `0..500` lexes as number, range,
number without a special case — the same yield the number lexer makes
in parser.zig:325.
A `-` opens a number only when a digit follows it; a lone `-` is the
unbind sentinel and a word (see #unbind). rill has no infix minus.
number.name: constant.numeric.rill

range.//: `..` is the range separator and appears nowhere else in the language. It must be tried before #member or `0..500` reads as a projection.
range.name: keyword.operator.range.rill

//: One rule for both spellings, because they are the same thing: a path
segment (`plane.drift.@self.k.tight`) and a projection off a name
(`stats.mana`) and the mid-chain sugar (`| .pos.x`) all reuse
`parseProjections`. A segment may be a number (`plane.ents.1.$tilt`)
and may carry the `-`/`/` joiners (`plane.tags.in-courtyard.count`).
A sigil segment (`.@self`, `.$tilt`) is left to #sigil, which is why
this does not try to swallow one.
The three relative stores, reserved so an operator can never shadow
one (`registry.isReservedWord`): `plane` the world, `row` the row
being swept, `slate` the row's register file for one tick. The
lookahead is what keeps this from firing on an operator or a stream
that happens to be spelled the same — a head is always followed by a
dot, because a store on its own is not a value.
path-head.name: support.class.plane.rill

//: The four sigils name rows of the STORE, never operators — refused at
registration for exactly that reason (registry.zig:599). Each is one
token with its sigil ON, which is what `$wind` and `@self` are in the
tokenizer, so the sigil is inside the scope rather than split off as
punctuation. A lone sigil is an inert `raw` token and is left alone.
`@self` is the one that is the language's own word: it resolves at
MOUNT, per instance, and it is the single path a `def` may name and
still travel (`checkDefReach`, 2026-09-08). It gets its own scope so
it reads differently from `@roaches` — because it means something
different.
`{l: 0.28}` and the colon-kwarg `at: row.pos` are the same shape and
get the same scope. NO whitespace is allowed before the colon, and
that is not tidiness: it is `colonOpensFold`'s rule read from the
other side. Allow a space and `near :k.tight` reads as a kwarg named
`near`, which is the exact failure the adjacency rule was written to
prevent in the parser.
Operator lookup tries the TWO-WORD form first (parser.zig:2717), so a
host registry seeded from (verb, subop) pairs maps one row to one
operator. `rbf` is rill core's only two-word family (`rbf through`,
`rbf bump`) and is the only one spelled out here.
A host's two-word verbs are NOT, and cannot be: `drift spawn` and
`along track` are the same two tokens, and only the registry knows
which is a sub-op and which is a stream. Guessing gets `along track
loop` wrong in every kernel that draws a curve, so the second word
stays an argument and the line still reads correctly. To add a family,
add an alternative to the group below — the shape is closed on
purpose, so a wrong list is a visible edit rather than a heuristic.
HEAD POSITION: the start of a statement, or straight after a `|`, a
`{` that opened a fan-out block, or a `(` that opened a predicate
section. That is where a word is a verb.
The negative lookahead `(?![\w.:/-])` is what keeps this off the
other four things that can stand there: a path (`plane.`), a
projection off a name (`stats.mana`), a record key (`{l:`) and the
second half of a joined name. A statement head that is a local `as`
name (`t | write plane.follow.t`) does land here and is scoped as a
verb — see the module note; the alternative is a semantic pass, and a
chain reads as a chain either way.
`defstmt := ["export"] "def" name "(" port* ")" ["on" plane] "=" body`
(parser.zig:1233). The context ends at the `=`, so a one-line def
(`def dbl(x) = x | mul 2`) hands its body back to the ordinary rules.
IT MAY SPAN LINES. The `$` in `end` used to be the whole story — a
signature could not wrap, so the newline was the other way out. Since
the width canon (2026-09-09) the parser accepts a break inside the
parens and the printer puts one port on each line past 88 columns,
which `kernels/roaches.rill` needs at 234. That works here with no
new rule, and for a reason worth naming rather than relying on:
#port-pack is itself a begin/end rule, and a NESTED one masks its
parent's `end` — so this `$` is never offered while the parens are
open, and the signature survives to the `)`. Gated as G7e, because a
property nobody wrote down is a property the next edit removes.
`export def` marks a definition visible to the HOST; rill has no
imports and no cross-file reference, so that is the whole of what
visibility can mean, and the pack is the one thing that survives the
parse that flattens the body away.
def-signature.name: meta.function.definition.rill

patterns.//: `on row` / `on plane` — the definition's own evaluation plane (2026-09-08). `on` reserves nothing: the parser looks for it in exactly one place, which is here.

//: The PARAMETER PACK (§3.9): a default that makes the port optional at
the call site, an advisory range that nothing enforces, and — through
the separate `describe` block — one sentence each. Blade3D's
`[OperatorParameter(…)]`, transposed: one declaration is the signature,
the widget, the documentation and the validation at once.
port-pack.name: meta.parameters.rill

patterns.//: `x: number` — the port's declared type. Types are interned freely, so any word may be one; `number`, `boolean`, `string` and `any` are the four the shape grammar also knows.

range-group.//: `(0..500)` — advice, not a constraint. A sane range for a slider and for a reader; nothing clamps and nothing refuses.
range-group.name: meta.range.rill

//: `describe <name>` opens the prose block an exported def is held to.
The block ends at a DEDENT (parser.zig:1549, `t.col <= kw.col`) and
blank lines inside it are skipped, so the `while` continues on an
indented line or an empty one and stops at the first line back in the
left margin.
The check runs both ways: an exported port with no line is refused,
and a line naming a port that does not exist is refused too — that one
for local defs as well, because a block that lies is wrong whoever
wrote it. So the port names here are scoped as parameters, not as the
statement heads they would otherwise look like.
describe-block.name: meta.describe.rill

comparison.//: `= != < <= > >=` are ordinary operators over data — there is no `if` statement and no exec wire (§4.3). `where (= 0)` and `| > 0.5` are the same six words.
comparison.name: keyword.operator.comparison.rill

unbind.//: A lone `-` is the console's unbind sentinel (`light arche l1 -`) and lexes as a WORD, because rill has no infix minus — subtraction is `sub`.
unbind.name: constant.language.unbind.rill

//: Everything else a name can be: an argument, a flag (`loop`, `desc`), a
keyword-introduced port's word (`radius 12`), a write mode (`hold`,
`add`, `stops`), a stream read by name, a bare word bound to a
string-typed port. `-` and `/` are name-INTERIOR when they join two
name characters, which is what makes `key-light` one entity name and
`render/grade/exposure` one knob path — and, in passing, what makes
the `//` comment rule sound.
bare-word.name: variable.other.rill
